For example, you are crossing the street and get hit by a car but you were texting on your phone at the time.  A jury can say that you were 20% at fault and the motorist was 80% at fault. I completely agree. The Jones Act is the sole reason for the very high cost of living here.

For those not familiar, the Jones Act is a protectionist law that says any ship traveling from a U.S. port to a U.S. port must be an American-made ship with a majority American crew. So, a ship bringing goods to the U.S. from China is not allowed to stop in Hawaii, drop off part of its load, then continue on to another U.S. port. Since Hawaii's demand for goods is small (relatively speaking) what this does is forces ships to go past Hawaii to drop their goods on the Mainland. And goods that need to then go to Hawaii are offloaded from that foreign-flagged ship, loaded onto another U.S. flagged ship and then sent to Hawaii. Since over 80% of U.S. goods carried over water are on foreign-flagged vessels, and U.S. ships are generally much more expensive to operate, this more than doubles shipping costs to the islands.
